neighbours.label: the end of a phrase describing someone leaving or walking away (walked out, walk away, watched him go)
fire: After the argument ended, Marcus grabbed his coat and walked out without a word.
She thanked the nurse, picked up her bag, and slowly walked away from the desk.
The old man tipped his hat to us and wandered off down the lane.
We stood on the porch and watched the stranger go until he vanished into the fog.
Without looking back, the boy turned around and ran out of the kitchen.
Tired of the noise, Helen got up from the table and left the room.
He muttered an apology, stepped back, and hurried away into the crowd.
Lisa closed the folder, nodded once, and strode out through the front door.
quiet: After the argument ended, Marcus grabbed his coat and sat down without a word.
She thanked the nurse, picked up her bag, and slowly read the form at the desk.
The old man tipped his hat to us and smiled at the children in the lane.
We stood on the porch and watched the rain fall until the fog grew thick.
Without looking up, the boy kept stirring the soup in the kitchen.
Tired of the noise, Helen turned up the radio at the table in the room.
He muttered an apology, stepped closer, and shook hands with the crowd.
Lisa closed the folder, nodded once, and handed it to the clerk at the desk.
